title: Unify shard key handling for event_stream and deploy partial indexes with online migration
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Problem: event_stream (huge multi-tenant table) currently uses two inconsistent columns to route tenant reads: tenant_shard_id (nullable) and shard_key_v2 (text). Several hot queries join on both, or use OR predicates, which defeats indexes and causes spike CPU during tenant-list operations. We see repeated p99 spikes (>3s) for control-plane list APIs and elevated IO during daily maintenance windows. Goal: consolidate routing to a single canonical shard key path, create compact partial indexes that cover the most common query shapes, and migrate rows online with zero downtime. This ticket covers schema refactor, index rollout, and an online backfill/migration plan with monitoring and rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: All control-plane list and join queries that previously used OR between tenant_shard_id and shard_key_v2 must be able to hit a single partial index path
p95 latency for tenant list endpoint reduces by at least 35% in staging and 20% in prod within two weeks of rollout
No full-table sequential scans observed for event_stream on production during normal traffic after indexes are live
Migration tool can backfill 100M rows at production throughput while respecting CPU throttle limits and completing within SLA window
Rollback plan validated in staging: ability to drop new indexes and revert to previous query plans without data loss
migration_plan: Add new column canonical_shard_key (VARCHAR) with default NULL and pg_catalog.security defers to application for writes
Deploy small PR that writes canonical_shard_key for all new/updated events (dual writes) — dump: app-level feature flag enabled
Create two partial indexes on event_stream: (canonical_shard_key, created_at) WHERE canonical_shard_key IS NOT NULL; and (tenant_id, event_type) WHERE canonical_shard_key IS NULL — both CONCURRENTLY
Run backfill job in k8s Batch: windowed workers that update canonical_shard_key for batches of primary keys with rate limiting; job emits progress to metrics gateway
Once backfill reaches 99.5% and low-error rate, flip query planner hint in db client layer to favor canonical_shard_key and remove OR predicates
Monitor for 48 hours, then schedule index consolidation: create covering index for historical queries and drop legacy indexes CONCURRENTLY
Remove dual-write code and drop tenant_shard_id legacy column in a future migration after a final verification window
rollout_steps: Stage 1 (Canary): Enable dual-write + new column in staging and preprod, run backfill for 24h and validate query plans
Stage 2 (Small prod): Enable dual-write for 10% traffic via routing flag, create partial indexes CONCURRENTLY during low traffic window, start backfill at low rate
Stage 3 (Full prod): Gradually increase backfill throughput, monitor CPU/IO and slow queries; if p99 regressions >10% revert traffic flag
Stage 4 (Cutover): Switch queries to canonical_shard_key predicate and retire OR path; re-evaluate index utility and drop old indexes CONCURRENTLY
Stage 5 (Cleanup): Remove dual-write after 2 weeks of stable metrics and schedule final column drop in subsequent release
notes: We observed that queries using OR cause planner to choose seqscan because statistics combine two highly skewed distributions. Partial indexes should give the planner a selective path.
Backfill will use primary key ranges and avoid touching recently updated rows by skipping rows with updated_at > backfill_start_time; ensures idempotency.
Consider using pg_repack or pg_partman later if bloat becomes an issue after schema churn. Not part of this ticket.
owner_oncall_runbook: If backfill task errors >5% for three consecutive hours, pause and investigate logs in k8s job pods
If seqscan_count on event_stream increases by >3x baseline, revert query flag and open DB incident
If p99 latency increases >25% after cutover, immediately revert to dual-write + OR predicate and create hotfix
